item.title: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona
item.description: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona Joao Cancelo has emerged as one of Alejandro Balde’s strongest supporters within the Barcelona dressing room, offering encouragement and advice as the defender struggles to establish himself under Hansi Flick. According to Mundo Deportivo , the Portuguese full-back has even defended his teammate in conversations with the German manager, while showing concern among senior players over Balde’s situation. The development comes amid uncertainty surrounding Balde’s Barcelona future. As previously reported, the academy graduate is increasingly open to leaving in January after struggling to secure regular playing time. In fact, despite Barcelona’s defensive injury problems, he has managed just 116 minutes across four appearances, raising questions about his standing in Flick’s plans. Cancelo takes Alejandro Balde under his wing Cancelo has emerged as Balde’s biggest supporter. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Cancelo’s support is, in fact, an interesting development given Balde’s initial reaction to his arrival at Barcelona. As per the outlet, the Spaniard struggled to understand the decision to sign another left-back, particularly as he was expected to be Flick’s first choice. As it turns out, however, their relationship has evolved, with the experienced Portuguese defender now regularly encouraging Balde, offering advice and reassuring him during a difficult period. It has even been suggested that Cancelo has also spoken to Flick in his teammate’s defence on at least one occasion. Another Barcelona senior player questions Flick As per the outlet, Cancelo is not the only senior figure concerned about how Flick has handled Balde, as another influential Barcelona player, who enjoys direct communication with the manager, also questioned one of his training decisions. Balde is likely to leave Barcelona in January. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The incident involved Flick changing Balde’s position during a training match. The teammate reportedly challenged the decision, questioning how the defender could demonstrate his abilities when he was not being trained in his natural position. What happens now? Notably, the situation adds to Balde’s increasingly difficult relationship with his role at Barcelona. Having spent most of his development at the club since joining the academy, he is now facing uncertainty over his long-term prospects. Now, with January approaching, the support of senior dressing-room figures could prove important, although unless his opportunities improve, Balde may still consider leaving to secure the regular football he wants.

item.title: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany
item.description: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ): Ex-Borussia Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela is confident Jürgen Klopp is the right man who can restore the German national team to it's former glory. “He is able to change the important things in a short matter of time, and that’s what makes him a good fit," Owomoyela said at a media round in Munich attended by Bulinews.com . “I wish he could have the Germany guys every day [to practice] but that’s not the case. As I said, he’s able to create an instant impact and a clear vision of what to do. “Now more than before, his reputation helps players believe what he is saying. All of that is a good fit for a coach with less time but can make things happen. “It’s just about finding the right people. He used a lot of players [in his first international period] and that will be the case going forward too," the Hamburg native added. Having played under Klopp at Dortmund for five seasons between 2008 and 2013, Owomoyela gave some fascinating insights into what the 59-year-old demands from his squad. “He was a coach who pushed for hard work but have fun while doing it. He always had fun it seemed, Even though he asked a lot of us, he would let us have fun as well. “He was the loudest in the dressing rooms, so he gave you that kind of freedom. But, you had to back it up on the pitch working hard and doing what he asked. “He could create pictures. He made it really easy to understands where he wanted you to go and what he wanted you to do. It was like a movie in your head. “So, that kind of ability to get you motivated to do what you need to do, it’s what puts him above many others. He wanted us to play the most intense football. "It was hunt, hunt, hunt, always hunt. If you got the ball, run fast at your opponent as hard as possible. If they [the opponent] got the ball, go hunt it [back] again. "He would play games too, if we ran 120 kilometres [as a team] one week, next week he would say let’s do 124 [kilometres]. We believed in what he was saying. “Even though we lost games and derbies, he would say it doesn’t matter because he felt we were going in the right direction,” he said, speaking with a undeniable passion. Perhaps the proof is in the pudding. During his time at a once lowly BVB side, he transformed them into a deadly force which claimed two Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal. Whether that can be replicated on the international stage is up for debate. However, in Owomoyela's mind, Klopp possesses the necessary traits to bring dreams into reality.

item.title: 'Absolutely embarrassing!' - Gary Neville slams Arsenal star Gabriel for 'play-acting' during Premier League victory over Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville has strongly criticised Arsenal defender Gabriel for his embarrassing play-acting during a vital Premier League victory over Liverpool at Anfield. The Brazilian went down clutching his face following a minor collision, prompting a fierce response from the former Manchester United captain on commentary. Gabriel criticised for Anfield theatrics Neville has accused Gabriel of embarrassing play-acting during Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool . Mikel Arteta's side secured a vital 1-0 win at Anfield to move three points clear at the top of the table. The controversy occurred in the opening minutes of the tense encounter following a physical collision between the Brazilian defender and Liverpool striker Alexander Isak. Gabriel immediately went down holding his face and appealed to referee Andy Madley for a foul. However, television replays quickly exposed the true nature of the incident involving the Arsenal centre-back. The footage clearly showed that Isak's arm had only made contact with Gabriel's upper chest rather than his face. Neville tears into the defender Neville was far from impressed with the theatrical reaction and voiced his frustration on Sky Sports commentary. The former United defender believes Gabriel must permanently remove this behaviour from his game. "He does let himself down at times," Neville stated. "I love his fire, his passion and his tenacity. But there’s a push into his upper chest and he goes down holding his face." Neville continued his assessment with a blunt final verdict on the Anfield incident. He added: "It’s absolutely embarrassing. He needs to stop doing that." Arsenal secure a massive away victory Despite the early controversy, Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game after 16 minutes to seal all three points. The narrow defeat was a bitter blow for Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, who remain fifth in the table and outside the Champions League places. Neville was quick to praise Arsenal for their resilience and tactical discipline following the final whistle. He highlighted the sheer magnitude of securing a clean sheet at such a notoriously difficult venue. "It was a defensive masterclass from Arsenal," Neville explained. "Andoni Iraola will be upset, he will feel like his team have given everything, but they put themselves right in the driving seat." European football returns for both clubs Arsenal must quickly shift their focus away from domestic matters as they prepare for a midweek European away trip. Arteta's men travel to the Czech Republic to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League, hoping to extend their excellent run of form. Liverpool also return to Champions League action in the coming days as they desperately look to bounce back from this frustrating league disappointment. Iraola will take his squad to Turkey for a highly challenging fixture against Fenerbahce.

item.title: 'It'll make us dizzy' - Gennaro Gattuso warns Lazio stars not to look at the Serie A table despite going top with comeback win over Cagliari
item.description: SS Lazio v Cagliari Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso has urged his players to ignore the Serie A standings despite moving clear at the summit with a 2-1 comeback win over Cagliari on Sunday. The Italian tactician insists his unbeaten side must remain grounded and prioritise reaching the 40-point mark after claiming a sixth consecutive league victory. Italian boss demands complete focus Gattuso refused to get carried away at the Stadio Olimpico even though the Biancocelesti sit top after 10 games for the first time since 2010-11. Sunday's triumph allowed the hosts to capitalise on Inter losing to AC Milan on Saturday . They have also recorded six straight league wins for the first time since Simone Inzaghi's reign in 2021. Late header seals comeback triumph Having netted 24 goals in their opening 10 fixtures for the first time since 2017-18, the hosts trailed to M'Bala Nzola's 20th-minute opener until Gustav Isaksen equalised in the 36th minute, setting the stage for substitute Andrea Pinamonti to head an 83rd-minute winner. Focusing on the club's 40-point target rather than the standings, Gattuso told DAZN Italia : "We are all up there, we still need 12 points to achieve the target of 40 that we set at the start of the season. "Every team in the league is balanced and well-structured, so we've got to keep taking it one game at a time and see where we end up. It is best that we don't look at the table right now, or it'll make us dizzy. We've got to push hard, rest, then push hard again." Unbeaten leaders show relentless spirit Alongside third-placed Roma, who sit four points behind under Gian Piero Gasperini, the leaders remain unbeaten in Serie A this season. Insisting his side must maintain their determination after responding to an earlier cup setback , Gattuso added: "That defeat didn't take away our belief in what we were doing, we don't let go. We work, we don't complain, this is the spirit that is pushing us on, because without that, we become a normal team." Crediting his substitutes for changing the contest against stubborn visitors, he continued: "It was a very difficult match and all credit for that goes to Cagliari, because we struggled and those who came off the bench changed the game with their mentality. This was a very important match for us, we did everything to take the result home. Cagliari are tough to deal with, they defend and attack well." Napoli test precedes international break Gattuso will now prepare his squad to face an out-of-form Napoli side in their final league match before the November international break. Maintaining their winning momentum will be vital as they seek to protect their cushion at the summit. Meanwhile, Cagliari must regroup quickly after suffering four straight top-flight defeats for the first time since April.

item.title: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick
item.description: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick Manchester United fans had to face up to another loss on Saturday afternoon, this time coming against Chelsea. Current situation Michael Carrick’s job appears safe until the next international break, which begins in a week, but he must navigate matches against AS Roma and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. It is widely expected that Carrick will lose his job in the not-too-distant future, with the side sitting seventeenth in the league, above the drop zone on goal difference. There have been numerous names linked to the Old Trafford hot seat, such as Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler. Nonetheless, one name that should also be one hundred percent on the club’s list is Unai Emery. Fabrizio Romano has stated that the club do in fact admire the Spaniard and he would be an incredible choice to replace Carrick. The case for Unai Emery Villa job The job Emery has done at Aston Villa is nothing short of spectacular. In the context of regularly having to sell his best players and failing to replace them with huge names, he continues to get his side firing. They won the Europa League last season and also finished fourth in the league. He has won 116 of his 211 matches at Aston Villa, boasting a win percentage of 55. The Spaniard is also a winner, as he has won five separate Europa Leagues: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and, of course, last season’s with Villa. Tactics What’s more, Emery is a strong tactician who regularly gets the best out of players. Villa lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins this summer, all crucial players to the first eleven. Most managers would crumble or throw their toys out of the pram. Emery’s response: second place in the Champions League with three wins from three. The league has been tougher going as they currently sit ninth, but showed their quality by beating Manchester City 2-1 two weekends ago. Emery has been described as a manager who is “the outstanding current example of the game-plan school: a stable structure underneath, an opponent-specific plan on top, and a depth of preparation that turns information into confidence.” He can be flexible and instructs his team to play with and without the ball with ease. The Spaniard is also famed for his tactical preparation, with “Emery’s weeks being built backwards from the opponent. Video analysis is the spine of preparation, hours of it, with the plan fed to players across the week through unit meetings, individual clips and walkthroughs rather than dumped on them the day before the game.” An itch to scratch at bigger clubs Finally, while it may be hard to see Emery walking away from the success he has built at Villa, he will have an itch to scratch at a truly massive football club. item.description: Kyler Murray became Minnesota's starting quarterback after leaving Arizona while Gardner Minshew was signed to be the Cardinals' back-up [Getty Images] The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend. There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime. The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again. Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. The Steelers improved to 6-2 and have now won four straight games, while the Browns dropped to 5-3. Brisker has quickly made his presence felt in Pittsburgh. The former second-round pick spent his first four seasons with the Chicago Bears before signing a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Steelers in March . item.title: Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers have a name for their version of the tush push . They call it the “Nittany Package,” a nod to tight end Pat Freiermuth’s Penn State background. Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 on Sunday. With five seconds left, the Steelers had the ball at the 1-yard line. Aaron Rodgers chose to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal. Freiermuth took the direct snap and followed center Zach Frazier into the end zone. Tight end Darnell Washington and running back Jaylen Warren pushed him from behind. It gave Pittsburgh a 20-6 lead and was Freiermuth’s first rushing touchdown in six NFL seasons. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCarthy said Rodgers made the call . “Aaron called that play,” McCarthy said. “Obviously, everybody agreed with it. But the whole mechanics leading up to that, I think that just shows the confidence they have and, obviously, Aaron’s experience of handling those situations.” The Steelers have used the Nittany Package four times and converted on every attempt. They previously ran it on fourth-and-1 against the Patriots and Colts, and on third-and-1 against the Bengals. Sunday was their first attempt from the goal line. According to Rodgers, he was not leaving the field without trying to score. Pittsburgh had no timeouts left, so a failed attempt would have ended the half. Troy Fautanu also called it his favorite play. Pittsburgh had earlier failed to score from the Browns’ 2-yard line and settled for a field goal. McCarthy said he wished he could have those three plays back. But the Nittany Package worked when the Steelers tried it again on Sunday. item.title: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho
item.description: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho Real Madrid have seen a massive turnaround in their fortunes in the last few weeks, making it six wins in a row with victory over Racing Santander. Los Blancos came flying out of the blocks at El Sardinero and scored three goals in the first half, which was enough for them to secure the three points. Among the many players who had a great game was Arda Guler, who continued his impressive start to the season. While Kylian Mbappe continues to dominate the goalscoring headlines, the Turkish international is quietly establishing himself as the creative spark of the team. Guler leads La Liga in two creative statistics Guler has registered 39 key passes and 21 accurate crosses this season, leading La Liga in both metrics. His numbers underline just how important and undroppable he has become for Jose Mourinho, making that right-wing position his own. The 21-year-old has also accumulated 4.32 expected assists (xA), the second-highest tally in the competition. His tally of 12 big chances created also places him second among La Liga players this season. Despite these numbers, the Turkish international has only three assists to his name, including one in the 3-0 victory over Racing. Against Racing, Guler provided a perfectly weighted through ball for Jude Bellingham’s well-taken goal. Three assists don’t paint the whole picture Guler’s underlying numbers suggest his influence and assist tally should have been much greater than just three. Expected assists is a measure of the quality of chances he has created, and the fact that his actual assists fall short of that figure suggests his teammates have not been clinical enough. Most leading assist providers in football tend to register more assists than their xA suggests, but Guler is an exception. Arda Guler has been Real Madrid’s creative force this season. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) However, if the finishing falls into place, it is encouraging that Guler’s underlying numbers are so promising. Mourinho trusts him a lot, and his ability to drift inside, identify passing lanes and deliver inch-perfect crosses provides the perfect balance for Madrid’s transitional attackers. Guler is also an exceptional set-piece taker, always posing a threat from both free kicks and corners. The 21-year-old is slowly evolving from a talented youngster into one of the first names on Mourinho’s team sheet , and it remains to be seen how he fares over the course of the season.

item.title: No Grealish, no cry - the rise of Everton's youngsters
item.description: Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season [Getty Images] As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high. A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes. Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training. The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years. Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney. A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley. Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career. After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves. The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season. David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground. "I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be]. "But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball. "But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair." While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season. item.description: Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2-1 at San Mamés on Sunday 1 November to end their rivals' run of four straight league wins. The visitors have formally disputed the first-half penalty that decided the derby, while Athletic lost another striker to injury. Every goal in the Bilbao derby arrived before half-time. Nico Williams provided the assist for the opening goal. Luka Sučić equalised on the half-hour. A crowd of 50,092 watched the game. Before kick-off, Unai Simón presented his Yashin Trophy to the home crowd. A minute’s silence was also held for the victims of the Urda rail accident. Real Sociedad dispute the penalty that settled the derby The visitors left Bilbao angry about the decisive spot-kick. In its official match report, Real Sociedad called it a penalty that never was and criticised VAR for not stepping in. The club statement added that the chip inside the match ball shows Jon Aramburu made contact with the ball in his challenge on Nico Williams. Pellegrino Matarazzo said that for him it was clearly not a penalty. The Real Sociedad coach could not understand why VAR had not intervened to cancel it. He was booked for dissent in the 65th minute, a minute after Mamadou Sarr received a yellow card for the same offence. Referee Alejandro Hernandez showed Real Sociedad four yellow cards in total, against two for Athletic. The statistics point in two directions. Real Sociedad dominated the ball, completing 514 accurate passes to Athletic’s 307. Terzić’s side created the clearer chances, however. Unai Simón made four saves, while Álex Remiro made one. Sučić was the highest-rated player on the pitch at 7.52. Athletic win but lose another striker The victory came at a cost. Maroan Sannadi felt his hamstring early in the game. Athletic will need one or two more days to know how long he will be out. His injury follows Gorka Guruzeta’s serious knee injury at Valencia on 17 October, which left the squad short of strikers. With 83 minutes on the pitch, Navarro created four key passes and was rated 7.2. The win was Athletic’s third in a row across all competitions, after a 6-1 victory over Prat and a 4-0 win against Getafe. They sit seventh, two points behind Sevilla. Real Betis are four points clear of Real Sociedad. Athletic also have a game in hand. Their matchday-eight fixture at Rayo Vallecano was suspended. Objects landed on the field during that game, among them paper planes and tiny balls made of silicone. Rayo were fined €6,000, the maximum sanction under the disciplinary code. The match will resume behind closed doors at Vallecas on Wednesday 9 December at 20:00. Real Sociedad return to action first, hosting Lyon in the Europa League league phase on Thursday 5 November. item.title: Julian Erosa Explains Retiring From UFC
item.description: Julian Erosa UFC Getty Long-time UFC featherweight fan favorite Julian Erosa explained why he made the decision to retire from mixed martial arts. Erosa laid down his gloves in the center of the Octagon following his first-round KO win over JeongYeong Lee at UFC Vegas 123, as he officially retired from the UFC with a final record of 10-9 inside the Octagon. Erosa had already announced before the fight that he was going to retire, so it wasn’t a surprise to see him hang up his gloves despite a terrific performance against Lee. So, why is Erosa retiring when he is seemingly still a UFC-caliber fighter? Julian Erosa Breaks Down Retirement Decision Speaking to reporters after UFC Vegas 123, Erosa broke down his decision to retire from MMA. “I was going back and forth in my mind: If I win the fight, I’m going to want to do it again because it’s the best feeling in the world. If I lose the fight, I’m going to want redemption. Win, lose or draw, I’m going to want to come back in here. So before I even got the fight, I told my wife, ‘This is going to be the last one,’ and be content with that decision. Once I was at ease with it and at peace with that decision, I could just go in the fight and just focus on it being a fight just like any other fight camp – focus on that and then be, I’m already happy with the decision of retiring. I didn’t want to be the guy that’s going to retire and then come back in a month. I’m happy with the way it turned out. I haven’t left any stone unturned. I made it from ‘Ultimate Fighter’ to Contender Series, been cut and rehired by the UFC so many times – I want to go out on my own terms,” Erosa said (via MMAjunkie.com ). Will Julian Erosa Compete Again? While Erosa did announce his retirement, it’s hard to take MMA fighters’ retirements at face value sometimes, as so many of them have hung up their gloves just to return a few years later. In Erosa’s case, it does feel like he’s done for good, as he has a young family to spend his time with. Not only that, but he was knocked out eight times in his career, so it is a smart decision to stop getting hit in the head anymore. item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Of all the things that have gone wrong with the Dallas Cowboys thus far in what appears to be another cursed NFL season, the steady disappearance of wide receiver George Pickens is low down on the list. But that’s not because it’s unworthy of attention or scrutiny–it’s just because there are so many other issues to consider, so many other failures to address. The defense, the coaching, the indecisive approach to personnel, it all adds up to an incredibly disappointing 2026 season that started with the Cowboys openly talking about a trip to the Super Bowl, a bit of bravado that looks ridiculous in hindsight, like a gambler buying a lottery ticket certain that the millions are coming soon. It’s easy to lose Pickens in that shuffle. On Sunday, in the dramatic 33-30 loss to the Cardinals in overtime, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott targeted Pickens only four times, and Pickens played only about 40 snaps, around where he was in Week 7. A defensive meltdown was the reason the Cowboys collapsed on Sunday, but it is impossible to ignore the fact that the Cowboys are, well, ignoring Pickens. Cowboys Cutting George Pickens Snaps Why that’s happening is a fair question. Last week, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer publicly called out Pickens for his lack of seriousness when it comes to blocking in the run game. Pickens saw his snaps drop thereafter. But this is the same receiver who posted 93 catches and 1,429 yards last year, who was hailed for having the best training camp of any player on the Cowboys roster, and who was clearly focused on a big season that would lead to a big payout in free agency next winter. None of it has happened. The Cowboys have Pickens, and they’re not using him. Cleverly, Dallas Morning News writer Joseph Hoyt compared Pickens to, “a subscription that the Cowboys forgot they signed up for.” And Hoyt writes that the Cowboys, who have Pickens on a one-year, $27 million franchise tag contract, should dump Pickens and pick up whatever draft asset they can. McKee, filling in for the injured Jalen Hurts, went 23-of-34 for 212 yards with an interception. Elijah Mitchell, elevated from the practice squad on Saturday , also got 11 carries. The 29-year-old is not the only Eagle taking accountability during the skid. Last week, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took the blame after the Dallas Cowboys ran for 204 yards in a 38-21 loss on Monday Night Football. The good news for Philadelphia is that the NFC East remains up for grabs. The New York Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, and the Eagles will host them at Lincoln Financial Field next Sunday. If Philadelphia hopes to salvage its season, the turnaround will need to start there.
